steps.subject: [InstCombine] Conditionally fold select i1 into and/or

evidence: Changes production InstCombine select-to-and/or canonicalization and thus can alter downstream binary operator shapes.
The transformation is poison/select-specific and neither invokes ValueTracking nor manipulates the PHI operand structure asserted by getInvertibleOperand.
features: boolean_canonicalization, instcombine_select, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine, path:llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine, poison_safety
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit makes InstCombine's i1 select-to-and/or conversion more selective in InstCombinerImpl::visitSelectInst. Instead of allowing the conversion whenever the unsafe-select option is enabled, it introduces IsSafeToConvert, which permits it when the alternative arm is implied poison, or, under the unsafe option, only when the arm cannot create poison and does not propagate poison from an operand that can create poison. The same gate is applied to both select true/false constant cases, and tests are updated to retain selects where and/or folding is no longer accepted.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitSelectInst; IsSafeToConvert; impliesPoison; canCreatePoison; propagatesPoison
Behavioral change: Restricts folding select i1 %cond, i1 true, i1 %false into an or-like form by requiring IsSafeToConvert(%false).; Restricts folding select i1 %cond, i1 %true, i1 false into an and-like form by requiring IsSafeToConvert(%true).; When unsafe select transforms are enabled, rejects an alternative arm that itself can create poison or that propagates poison from an operand that can create poison.; Updates tests to expect retained select instructions instead of and/or in poison-sensitive boolean and comparison patterns.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine overlaps with the reported optimization subsystem.; The crash assertion is in ValueTracking::getInvertibleOperand and checks BO1->getOperand(*Idx) == PN1 && BO2->getOperand(*Idx) == PN2.; No retrieved hunk directly references ValueTracking, getInvertibleOperand, PHINode operand matching, or that assertion.
Reproducer link: The changed tests cover i1 selects, boolean and/or forms, shifts, comparisons, widenable conditions, and poison-sensitive transforms.; The retrieved evidence does not establish that the compact C -O2 reproducer contains these select-to-and/or patterns or reaches this conversion.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; poison analysis used by InstCombine
Causal explanation: This is an implementation change in the affected InstCombine subsystem and it changes the binary boolean IR shapes that later optimizations may observe. In particular, it can prevent creation of and/or BinaryOperators from selects. However, the asserted failure concerns a specific ValueTracking invertible-operand relationship involving binary operators and PHI nodes, while the shown change neither invokes that analysis nor constructs or edits PHIs. The causal link is therefore indirect and unsupported beyond subsystem overlap.
Causal confidence: 0.16
Build risk: Production InstCombine logic changes together with multiple regression-test expectation updates.; Tests explicitly demonstrate changed canonical output from and/or to select, so downstream tests depending on prior canonicalization may need adjustment.; No build-system changes are shown.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit adds InstCombine regression tests for scalable-vector transformations: narrowing an extended floating-point splat through fadd, scalable-vector truncation and allocation bitcasts, and preventing an invalid scalar bitcast fold after insertelement for both undef and poison inputs. The retrieved hunks are entirely test files and contain no production LLVM implementation change.
Changed symbols: shrink_splat_scalable_extend; trunc_nxv2i64_to_nxv2i32; bitcast_of_insert_i8_i16; InstCombine scalable-vector regression checks
Behavioral change: Adds expected InstCombine output checks for scalable floating-point splat shrinking, scalable truncation, and fixed/scalable allocation casts.; Adds negative checks requiring InstCombine not to fold bitcast(insert <vscale x 1 x i16> ..., i16 %val, 0) into a direct bitcast of the scalar value for scalable vectors.; Does not change compiler production behavior in the retrieved hunks; it only constrains and documents expected behavior through tests.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine is the only direct subsystem overlap.; No retrieved hunk mentions ValueTracking, getInvertibleOperand, BO1->getOperand, or the reported assertion.
Reproducer link: The added tests exercise scalable-vector casts, shuffles, truncations, and SVE-related IR rather than the reported compact C -O2 reproducer.; No reproducer behavior matching the ValueTracking invertible-operand assertion is shown.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine test suite
Causal explanation: Although the tests are in the InstCombine area, the candidate contains no implementation changes that could alter clang -O2 execution or cause the ValueTracking assertion. The scalable-vector test patterns also provide no evidence of the PHI/binary-operator operand relationship asserted by getInvertibleOperand.
Causal confidence: 0.00
Build risk: Test-only change; no build-system or production-source modifications are shown.; New tests invoke opt -instcombine and FileCheck, so they can expose existing InstCombine output regressions.; Several tests use scalable-vector and AArch64 SVE intrinsic IR, making their test coverage target-feature-specific.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Extends InstCombine's foldICmpShrConstant to fold comparisons of shifted values against zero into direct unsigned range comparisons on the unshifted operand. Equality-to-zero becomes an unsigned-less-than comparison using (C + 1) shifted by the shift amount, while the non-equality path becomes unsigned-greater-than using the corresponding upper bound minus one. Tests update multi-use logical/arithmetic shift cases and dependent phase-ordering output.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::foldICmpShrConstant; ICmpInst; lshr_eq_0_multiuse; lshr_ne_0_multiuse; ashr_eq_0_multiuse; ashr_ne_0_multiuse; with_range; ctlz_loop_with_abs
Behavioral change: For a shifted value compared with zero, foldICmpShrConstant now replaces an equality comparison with an ICMP_ULT directly on X against (C + 1) << ShAmtVal.; For the corresponding non-equality case, it replaces the comparison with ICMP_UGT directly on X against ((C + 1) << ShAmtVal) - 1.; The transform applies even where the shifted result has multiple uses, as demonstrated by the updated multi-use shift tests.; The changed output can remove a shift-and-compare pattern and expose direct arithmetic range comparisons to subsequent InstCombine and analysis steps.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine; ValueTracking; getInvertibleOperand; BO1->getOperand
Reproducer link: The issue reproduces under Clang -O2 as an assertion in ValueTracking::getInvertibleOperand.; This commit changes arithmetic comparison IR produced by InstCombine, but no retrieved test or hunk ties the reported testcase to shift-vs-zero comparison folding.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; integer shift comparison folding; arithmetic range comparisons
Causal explanation: This candidate directly changes InstCombine arithmetic IR and introduces new direct comparisons over the original operand, a closer structural match to optimizer/value-reasoning concerns than the call-convention or undef-only changes. Such rewritten compare/shift patterns could alter the inputs reaching ValueTracking's invertible-operand reasoning. Nevertheless, it does not modify ValueTracking, does not mention getInvertibleOperand, and the provided crash signal is text-unreachable; therefore the link remains plausible but unproven.
Causal confidence: 0.28
Build risk: The implementation change has targeted InstCombine regression coverage for lshr/ashr equality and non-equality cases.; Additional test updates cover a range-metadata-derived arithmetic case and a phase-ordering loop case, indicating the transform affects downstream optimization output.; No build-system or interface changes are visible; risk is primarily semantic correctness of the new unsigned bounds and interactions with later InstCombine folds.

Summary: This commit reverts an InstCombine fold for comparisons of shifted values against zero. It removes the special zero-constant branch in foldICmpShrConstant that converted equality and inequality tests on a shift result into unsigned range comparisons on the original input, and updates tests to retain comparisons against the shifted or masked values.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::foldICmpShrConstant; ICmpInst; CmpInst::ICMP_EQ; ConstantInt::get
Behavioral change: Removes the zero-comparison rewrite that changed shifted-value equality to an ICMP_ULT range test on the unshifted operand.; Removes the corresponding inequality rewrite to ICMP_UGT.; Preserves icmp eq/ne comparisons against multi-use shift or mask results in the shown regression tests rather than replacing them with range comparisons.
Assertion or trace link: getInvertibleOperand; ValueTracking; BO1->getOperand(*Idx) == PN1 && BO2->getOperand(*Idx) == PN2; InstCombine
Reproducer link: The reported failure occurs at Clang -O2, where InstCombine is relevant.; The changed optimization affects compare and arithmetic-expression shape, including a shown signed-division-with-range regression test.; No retrieved hunk mentions getInvertibleOperand, ValueTracking, or the reported compact C testcase.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM InstCombine; Shift and integer-comparison simplification; ValueTracking only as a possible downstream consumer of the changed comparison IR
Causal explanation: Removing this fold changes the compare graph presented to later optimizations: instead of a direct range comparison over the shift input, InstCombine can leave a comparison over the shift or mask result. Such shape changes can theoretically alter whether ValueTracking attempts invertible-operand reasoning. selection.diff_summary:

The change introduces a bitwise-not/xor before ctpop for scalar and vector cases and updates tests to expect the new form while retaining nonmatching and extra-use cases.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitSub; sub_ctpop; sub_ctpop_vec; ctpop1_multiuse

top_candidates.subject: [InstCombine] relax masking requirement for truncated funnel/rotate match
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: InstCombine relaxes narrow funnel-shift/rotate recognition after a truncation by requiring known-zero high bits only for the right-shifted input. It no longer requires the left-shifted input to be masked, because high bits produced by that side are discarded by the final truncation. The newly accepted patterns are rewritten to narrow llvm.fshr intrinsics, as reflected by funnel and rotate regression tests.

Summary: This revert removes the zero-constant branch in InstCombine's shift-compare folding, so comparisons of shifted values against zero are no longer rewritten into unsigned range comparisons of the unshifted input. The associated tests change expected output from icmp ult/ugt range checks back to icmp eq/ne on the shift result, including multi-use lshr/ashr cases and a loop phase-ordering case.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::foldICmpShrConstant; lshr_eq_0_multiuse; lshr_ne_0_multiuse; ashr_eq_0_multiuse; ashr_ne_0_multiuse; with_range; ctlz_loop_with_abs
Behavioral change: Removes the fold of '(shift X, ShAmt) == 0' into 'X ult ((0 + 1) << ShAmt)'.; Removes the corresponding '!= 0' fold into an unsigned-greater-than comparison.; Preserves direct comparisons against the shifted result rather than introducing range-comparison arithmetic on the original operand.
Assertion or trace link: getInvertibleOperand; ValueTracking; InstCombine; BO1->getOperand(*Idx) == PN1 && BO2->getOperand(*Idx) == PN2

Pass or subsystem link: LLVM InstCombine; InstCombine compare simplification; ValueTracking is the assertion subsystem but is not modified by this commit

top_candidates.subject: Revert "[instcombine] Exploit UB implied by nofree attributes"
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This revert removes an InstCombine optimization in visitFree that treated freeing a pointer constrained by nofree attributes as undefined behavior, inserted an equality-to-null llvm.assume, and erased the free call. The prior behavior of retaining the free call is restored, along with tests that no longer expect the inserted assumptions.
Changed symbols: InstCombinerImpl::visitFree; CallInst; Attribute::NoFree; Builder.CreateICmpEQ; Builder.CreateAssumption; eraseInstFromFunction
Behavioral change: Stops inferring that a pointer passed to free must be null solely from argument, call-site, or function nofree attributes.; Stops inserting llvm.assume(pointer == null) or llvm.assume(false) for the affected free calls.; Retains free calls that the reverted optimization would have erased.
Assertion or trace link: The issue assertion is ValueTracking.cpp:getInvertibleOperand with an operand-identity condition involving BO1->getOperand and BO2->getOperand.; This commit does not modify ValueTracking, getInvertibleOperand, arithmetic operand matching, or the asserted operand relationship.
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O2 Clang assertion crash.; The retrieved change concerns free calls and nofree pointer attributes; no evidence ties the compact C reproducer to allocation, free, or nofree semantics.
Pass or subsystem link: LLVM InstCombine; Pointer/free-call and nofree-attribute simplification
Causal explanation: Although this commit is in InstCombine, it changes pointer-lifetime and UB assumptions around free rather than invertible arithmetic operands or ValueTracking simplification. The retrieved evidence provides no plausible direct path to the getInvertibleOperand assertion beyond general participation in the same optimization pass.
Causal confidence: 0.03
Build risk: The implementation removal is accompanied by updated InstCombine malloc/free/delete test expectations.; The test comments explicitly say the reverted transforms were thought legal but had previously been reverted because of difficult-to-isolate fallout.; One hunk was omitted, and no build or crash-reproduction result is supplied.

diff --git a/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstructionCombining.cpp b/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstructionCombining.cpp
index 724e2122ff60..fc10757dc1ed 100644
--- a/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstructionCombining.cpp
+++ b/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstructionCombining.cpp
@@ -2802,19 +2801,0 @@ Instruction *InstCombinerImpl::visitFree(CallInst &FI) {
-  
-  // If we free a non-null pointer we've been explicitly told won't be freed,
-  // this would be full UB and thus we can conclude that the argument must
-  // be null at the point of the free. Cases:
-  // 1) freeing a pointer which is explicitly nofree
-  // 2) calling free from a call site marked nofree (TODO: can generalize
-  //    for non-arguments)
-  // 3) calling free in a function scope marked nofree (when we can prove
-  //    the allocation existed before the start of the function scope)
-  if (auto *A = dyn_cast<Argument>(Op->stripPointerCasts()))
-    if (A->hasAttribute(Attribute::NoFree) ||
-        FI.hasFnAttr(Attribute::NoFree) ||
-        FI.getFunction()->hasFnAttribute(Attribute::NoFree)) {
-      Value *Null = ConstantPointerNull::get(cast<PointerType>(A->getType()));
-      Value *Cond = Builder.CreateICmpEQ(A, Null);
-      Builder.CreateAssumption(Cond);
-      return eraseInstFromFunction(FI);
-    }

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends ValueTracking's getInvertibleOperand logic to look through pairs of simple PHI recurrences in isKnownNonEqual reasoning. When two PHIs are in the same block and both match simple recurrences, it recursively checks whether their recurrence update binary operators have the same invertible operand relationship, then maps that recurrence operand back to the corresponding PHI incoming start operand. The added tests verify that comparisons between unequal add, subtract, multiply, shift-left, logical-shift-right, and arithmetic-shift-right recurrences fold to false.
Changed symbols: getInvertibleOperand; matchSimpleRecurrence; isKnownNonEqual; recurrence_add_neq; recurrence_add_neq_phi_order; recurrence_sub_neq; recurrence_mul_neq; recurrence_shl_neq
Behavioral change: getInvertibleOperand now handles Instruction::PHI operands by recognizing paired simple recurrences in the same basic block.; The new PHI case recursively queries getInvertibleOperand on the two recurrence update BinaryOperators.; If the recursive result identifies operand 0 as the invertible recurrence-carried operand, the code maps that result to the corresponding PHI start incoming operand according to each PHI's incoming-edge order.; ValueTracking can consequently prove more recurrence values non-equal, enabling folds of recurrence comparisons such as icmp eq of two add recurrences with distinct starts to false.
Assertion or trace link: getInvertibleOperand; llvm/lib/Analysis/ValueTracking.cpp; BO1->getOperand(*Idx) == PN1 && BO2->getOperand(*Idx) == PN2; ValueTracking; InstCombine
Reproducer link: The reported failure is an -O2 assertion in getInvertibleOperand.; This commit adds the exact asserted expression reported by the crash signal.; The added tests exercise PHI-based arithmetic recurrences and demonstrate new ValueTracking-driven folding of recurrence comparisons, although the supplied C reproducer itself is not available in the retrieved evidence.

evidence: Changes InstCombine output by replacing an unreachable result with nullness assumptions for free(nullptr).

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This InstCombine change corrects handling of free on a nofree pointer: because free(nullptr) is valid, the optimizer no longer treats every free of a nofree pointer as unreachable. Instead, visitFree emits an equality comparison with null and an llvm.assume requiring the argument to be null; a nonnull nofree argument still simplifies to assume(false). The accompanying tests update expected output from an unreachable marker to nullness assumptions.

Summary: This change registers the GNU memalign library function as an AlignedAllocLike allocation routine in MemoryBuiltins. That lets existing allocation analysis recognize memalign's alignment and size argument positions, enabling InstCombine to infer alignment and dereferenceable-or-null call attributes; regression coverage is added for constant, nonzero dynamic, possibly-zero dynamic, and unknown-alignment memalign cases.

top_candidates.subject: [AArch64][SVE][InstCombine] Replace last{a,b} intrinsics with extracts...
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit adds an AArch64 TargetTransformInfo InstCombine hook for SVE lasta and lastb intrinsics. The new instCombineSVELast recognizes a null predicate for lasta or selected constant ptrue predicate patterns, derives a fixed lane index, checks that it is within the scalable vector's minimum element count, and replaces the intrinsic with an extractelement instruction. A new AArch64 InstCombine test checks these replacements.
Changed symbols: instCombineSVELast; AArch64TTIImpl::instCombineIntrinsic; AArch64TTIImpl::getIntrinsicInstrCost; lasta_extractelement_0; lasta_extractelement_8; lastb_extractelement_0; lastb_extractelement_1; lastb_extractelement_2
Behavioral change: Adds AArch64TTIImpl::instCombineIntrinsic handling for aarch64_sve_lasta and aarch64_sve_lastb.; Replaces lasta with extractelement index 0 when its predicate is a null constant.; For recognized aarch64_sve_ptrue patterns vl1 through vl8 and vl16, converts lastb to extraction of the last active lane and lasta to extraction of the following lane.; Refuses the replacement when the derived lane index is not below the predicate vector's minimum number of elements.; Uses InstCombiner::replaceInstUsesWith after inserting the replacement extractelement before the intrinsic.
Assertion or trace link: InstCombine; getInvertibleOperand (assertion site, not modified); ValueTracking.cpp (assertion source, not modified)
Reproducer link: The issue is a generic compact-C Clang -O2 assertion crash; the visible transform requires AArch64 SVE lasta/lastb intrinsics and specific SVE predicates, none of which are present in the supplied reproducer description.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; AArch64 TargetTransformInfo; AArch64 SVE intrinsics
Causal explanation: The commit does execute through InstCombine, but the visible transform is narrowly target- and intrinsic-specific: it replaces selected AArch64 SVE lasta/lastb calls with extractelement. It does not alter ValueTracking or the binary-operator/PHI operand correspondence asserted by getInvertibleOperand. A connection would require the failing input to contain the relevant AArch64 SVE intrinsic pattern and for the newly created extract to lead indirectly to the ValueTracking assertion; neither condition is evidenced by the retrieved hunks or crash signal.
Causal confidence: 0.03
Build risk: The interface declaration in AArch64TargetTransformInfo.h and implementation in AArch64TargetTransformInfo.cpp are added together.; The implementation adds an explicit InstCombiner header include for the new hook use.; A dedicated opt -instcombine FileCheck test covers the new SVE intrinsic-to-extractelement rewrites.

+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1

+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1

+; Was pr49856.  We can match the recurrence without a loop
+; since dominance collapses in unreachable code.  Conceptually,
+; this is a recurrence which only executes one iteration.
+define void @nonloop_recurrence() {
+; CHECK-LABEL: 'nonloop_recurrence'
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Classifying expressions for: @nonloop_recurrence
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> %tmp U: [1,-2147483648) S: [0,-2147483648)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> (1 + %tmp)<nuw> U: [1,-2147483647) S: [1,-2147483647)
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Determining loop execution counts for: @nonloop_recurrence
+;
+bb:
+  br label %bb1
+
+bb1:                                              ; preds = %bb3, %bb
+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %bb ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+  ret void
+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1
+}
+

+; it's trip count simply doesn't relate to the single iteration
+; "recurrence" we found.

+; CHECK-NEXT:    --> (1 + %tmp)<nuw> U: [1,-2147483647) S: [1,-2147483647) Exits: <<Unknown>> LoopDispositions: { %loop: Variant }
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Determining loop execution counts for: @nonloop_recurrence_2
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: <multiple exits> Unpredictable backedge-taken count.
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: Unpredictable max backedge-taken count.
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Loop %loop: Unpredictable predicated backedge-taken count.
+;
+bb:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  br label %bb1
+bb1:                                              ; preds = %bb3, %loop
+  %tmp = phi i32 [ 2, %loop ], [ %tmp2, %bb3 ]
+  %tmp2 = add nuw nsw i32 %tmp, 1
+  br label %loop
+
+bb3:                                              ; No predecessors!
+  br label %bb1
+}
